paras: Bachia barbouri, also known commonly as Barbour's bachia, is a species of lizard in the family Gymnophthalmidae. The species is endemic to  Peru.
The specific name, barbouri, is in honor of American herpetologist Thomas Barbour.
B. barbouri is found in northwestern Peru, in the valleys of the Río Chinchipe, the Río Marañón, and the Río Utcubamba.
The preferred natural habitat of B. barbouri is forest.

The holotype of B. barbouri has a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of 5.6 cm (2.2 in). The legs are much reduced. The front leg is short, with only two digits. The back leg is either a small tubercle or is absent.
B. barbouri is oviparous. Each egg measures about 5 mm × 15 mm (0.20 in × 0.59 in).
